source.title: Helen: Optimizing CTR Prediction Models with Frequency-wise Hessian Eigenvalue Regularization
source.authors: Zi-Rui Zhu; Yong Liu; Zangwei Zheng; Hui-Feng Guo; Yang You

record.tranche_reason: Tests an optimizer and sharpness analysis in CTR prediction, a new task setting for the claim’s generalization topic.
record.gate_note: The paper compares CTR performance across optimizers and measures Hessian eigenvalues and their correlation with feature frequency. It does not report training error, a training–test gap, random-label fitting, or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7. Detailed per-model optimizer scores are in Tables 2, 3, and 6; aggregate comparisons are extracted below.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop Helen and evaluates CTR performance and feature-wise Hessian eigenvalues. It tests none of V1–V8: there is no plain SGD comparator for V4, and neither magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance nor training–test gaps for V7. A new task alone does not make this T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' conclusion: feature frequency correlates positively with embedding Hessian eigenvalues, and Helen reduces these eigenvalues while improving CTR benchmark performance. Their interpretation that this steers training toward more generalizable minima is not established through measured training–test gaps. Their claim of winning 20 of 21 experiments is inconsistent with the per-model AUC tables.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a frequency-wise perturbation optimizer for CTR models; compares with Adam, Nadam, Radam, SAM, and ASAM on benchmark datasets rather than reproducing the claim’s specified experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the optimizer performance; the paper reports inconsistent results for some baselines across Avazu, Criteo, and Taobao.

fits_no_version.finding: Helen increases mean CTR AUC over Adam on Avazu, Criteo, and Taobao and lowers mean feature-embedding Hessian-block top eigenvalues for PNN and DeepFM on Criteo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency-wise perturbation regularization can improve CTR benchmark performance while reducing feature-embedding Hessian sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM lowers mean feature-embedding Hessian-block top eigenvalues for PNN and DeepFM on Criteo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can reduce feature-embedding Hessian sharpness in CTR models.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-frequency correlations with Hessian-block top eigenvalues range from 0.700 to 0.977 across the six model-by-dataset combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More frequent categorical features tend to have larger embedding Hessian-block top eigenvalues in the tested CTR models.

record.problems: The study does not measure training error or a train–test gap, so its results cannot directly establish the claim’s generalization-gap relation. Reported optimizer comparisons use CTR AUC and LogLoss; the eigenvalue analysis is reported for PNN and DeepFM on Criteo, and uncertainty for the main table scores is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-model optimizer scores in Tables 2, 3, and 6 are not individually transcribed; the study reports seven models per optimizer and dataset, which would exceed the 60-row cap alongside the aggregate results. No results are omitted from the extracted eigenvalue-frequency correlation table.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning regimes. All evaluated optimizers use adaptive learning rates; SGD appears only as an illustrative underlying update in pseudocode.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons, training-set size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions, not judgments that the reported CTR improvements or eigenvalue reductions are unreadable. No omitted result tests a listed version. ASAM's weight-scaled perturbations are an optimizer component here, not a measurement of V7's gap-ranking relationship.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
The specified magnitude-aware perturbation measure and its ranking of training–test gaps; the study reports Hessian eigenvalues and CTR performance, not training–test error gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.measure: Pearson correlation r(λ, N), respectively for PNN and DeepFM
rows.note: The paper reports these correlations by dataset and model. They link frequency with Hessian eigenvalues, not eigenvalues with a measured training–test gap.
rows.check: Values match Table 1, but combine six model-by-dataset results that should be separate rows. The outcome is correlation with feature frequency, not generalization gap. Section 3.2 and excerpt E1 incorrectly claim every coefficient exceeds 0.8; PNN gives 0.759 and 0.700 on Avazu and Criteo.
